xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3423: Redesign SystemHealthPill popover: attention-grouped reasons, metered vitals, actionable agent alerts

plan.title: Redesign SystemHealthPill popover: attention-grouped reasons, metered vitals, actionable agent alerts
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: The SystemHealthPill popover presents its most important information — what needs the operator's attention right now — as a flat, undifferentiated bullet list: informational disclaimers sit at the same weight as stall alerts, identical warnings repeat verbatim once per agent, durations render as raw minutes (2946 instead of 49 h), no row names the agent, and no row offers an action. Metric tiles are text-only, three low-value tiles each consume a full grid row, and Top consumers rows have no proportional size cue.
narratives.Proposal: Redesign the popover per the operator-approved mockup (2026-08-01): a state badge + one-sentence summary answering 'do I need to do anything?', metered 2x2 vitals tiles, a chip row for admitted-agents/containers/relay, a Needs-attention section with severity-dotted rows that group identical-code agent reasons behind a xN badge and carry Open/Kill actions, a collapsed context-notes disclosure for severity:info reasons, and Top-consumers rows with kind badges, proportional memory bars, and LEAKED tags. Grouping/humanization logic lives in a new pure module src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/system-health-attention.ts. Server-side, agent-inactivity reasons name the agent and humanize the duration at emission (src/lib/agents/health.ts) so every consumer benefits. No contract/schema changes.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No contract or schema changes: packages/contracts/src/system-health.ts is untouched.
- No changes to health-state derivation/evaluate.ts; stalled keeps server severity 'warning' (red dot is a frontend-only mapping).
- No changes to HealthDashboard beyond it automatically benefiting from the FR-3 server copy change.
- No live ticker for the relative updated time; a static per-render relative value is sufficient.
- No popover width, position, Escape, or outside-click behavior changes (NFR-3).
- Do not touch the 'produced no activity' warm-resume copy in src/lib/cloister/deacon-review-signals.ts.
- Do not commit or move the gitignored mockup at .tmp/system-health-panel-redesign-mockup.html.
- Do not reimplement the kill flow; reuse the existing KillButton.

autoDecisions.summary: Co-locate the attention-model unit test at src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/system-health-attention.test.ts instead of tests/unit/frontend/
autoDecisions.rationale: The frontend vitest project only includes src/** under the frontend tree and excludes **/tests/**; co-location matches the dominant convention and keeps the happy-dom environment and fixture pattern.

autoDecisions.summary: Add new message assertions in agent-health.test.ts rather than updating existing message tests
autoDecisions.rationale: grep shows no test asserts the old 'produced no activity' message text; existing cases assert only reason.code via toMatchObject.

autoDecisions.summary: Open action uses the dashboard store's openIssue(issueId) and closes the popover
autoDecisions.rationale: store.ts:184 openIssue is the same navigation target the dashboard uses everywhere; no router machinery exists for a direct push.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep server severity 'warning' for agent.runtime.inactive.stalled; map it to critical presentation frontend-only
autoDecisions.rationale: NFR-1 forbids derivation changes; the approved design's red dot for stalled is presentational, keyed on reason.code in the attention module.

autoDecisions.summary: Grouped xN rows render no Kill/Open actions
autoDecisions.rationale: A group has no single kill or navigation target; the sub-line names the agents, and singleton rows carry the actions.

autoDecisions.summary: Docs item adds (not rewrites) a popover description in docs/RESOURCE-GOVERNOR.md
autoDecisions.rationale: Verified 2026-08-01: the doc references SystemHealthPill only in the inotify surfaces line and has no popover-layout description to rewrite; no Mintlify page covers the component.

Frontend: pure attention-model module with grouping, context notes, and summary line

expected_outputs: system-health-attention.test.ts passes covering grouping, context notes, sort order, and both summary variants

narrative.Action: Create src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/system-health-attention.ts exporting interface AttentionItem { severity: 'critical' | 'warning'; code: string; title: string; sub: string; agents: string[]; agentId?: string } and three pure functions: buildAttentionItems(snapshot), contextNotes(snapshot) (returns exactly the severity:'info' reasons), and summaryLine(snapshot, items). Grouping: key = reason.code; ONLY agent-domain reasons group — host/admission/service reasons are singletons titled by the reasonLabel() mapping extracted from SystemHealthPill.tsx:77-123 (move it into this module; keep exactly one copy and update the component import). Agent-domain reasons resolve their agent via snapshot.agents by position (agents[i].reasons belongs to agents[i]). Singleton agent rows title as '<agentId> · <issueId>' when AgentHealthSnapshot.issueId is set. Presentation severity: 'critical' when reason.severity is critical OR code is 'agent.runtime.inactive.stalled' (frontend-only mapping; server keeps 'warning'); else 'warning'. agentId is set only when exactly one agent groups into the row. Sort: critical first, then warning; within a severity, stalled before idle. summaryLine synthesizes the FR-8 sentence from item counts + host.metrics.memoryUsedPercent + admission.availableMemoryBytes; a snapshot with no items produces the all-clear variant naming spawn headroom, relay state, and zero stalled agents. Add co-located unit tests at src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/system-health-attention.test.ts following the createSnapshot() fixture pattern from SystemHealthPill.test.tsx:48.

Popover header: state badge, relative updated time, summary line, and chip row

Vitals tiles: meter bars, threshold colors, swap historical sub-label

narrative.Action: In SystemHealthPill.tsx vitals tiles (lines 364-384), add a 4px meter bar under each of the four tile values (CPU, Memory, Overdeck share, Swap). Bar width is the metric's percent of full (Memory uses host.metrics.memoryUsedPercent; CPU cpuPercent; Swap swapUsedPercent; Overdeck share overdeckMemoryPercent). Bar color: green below 60%, amber 60-85%, red above 85% for CPU/memory/swap; the Overdeck-share bar is neutral blue (attribution, not pressure). A null metric renders 'Unavailable' with NO bar — never a zero bar (null is not zero, contract comment system-health.ts:47-50). Add the swap sub-label 'historical · not live pressure' with an inline info marker.

items.title: Each vitals tile renders a meter bar whose width matches the metric percent and whose color follows the 60/85 thresholds (Overdeck bar neutral blue)

The swap tile renders the sub-label 'historical · not live pressure'
Needs-attention section replaces the bullet list, with context-notes disclosure and row actions

narrative.Action: Replace the flat bullet list (SystemHealthPill.tsx:401-407) with the Needs-attention section: one severity-dotted row per AttentionItem from buildAttentionItems() (red dot critical, amber warning), grouped rows showing a xN count badge with agent names in the sub-line. Below the rows render a closed-by-default <details> disclosure titled 'N context notes — background, not pressure signals' containing every contextNotes() reason (FR-1). Singleton agent rows (agentId set) with an issueId render an Open action that calls the dashboard store's openIssue(issueId) (src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/store.ts:184) and closes the popover. Render the existing KillButton on a singleton agent row only when a topConsumers entry matches (killTarget?.kind === 'agent' && killTarget.agentId === item.agentId, fallback consumer.id === item.agentId) — grouped xN rows render NO Kill/Open (no single target). Healthy state: the section is replaced by a single all-clear row (FR-8). Reuse KillButton (lines 157-233); do not reimplement the kill flow.
